excerpt_i18n.en: Over the past two years, traditional communication businesses have seen slowing growth, prompting telecom operators to collectively turn their focus to AI computing power. China Telecom, China Mobile, and China Unicom have successively announced large-scale plans for building intelligent computing centers, with the proportion of computing power investment in capital expenditure rising year by year. In this wave of transformation, the choice of computing chips by operators not only determines the cost structure of their own computing businesses but also significantly influences the direction of the domestic computing power industry. Currently, the domestic AI computing industry has seen a prosperous landscape with multiple technical routes such as TPU, GPU, and ASIC advancing in parallel. In building intelligent computing, operators are gradually moving away from solely relying on GPU solutions and opening up to more diversified computing power options. Particularly under the dual impetus of policy guidance for self-reliance and rapid iteration of domestic chip capabilities, domestic computing power has moved from laboratory validation to large-scale deployment. As the largest builders and operators of computing infrastructure in China, operators' selection decisions serve both as a capability test and a market window for the domestic computing power industry. During the 2026 World Artificial Intelligence Conference, the first domestic TPU intelligent computing cluster with a thousand cards was inaugurated in Hangzhou, East China. This project was jointly built by Zhonghao Xin Ying, Hangzhou Telecom, and ZTE. The first phase deploys 1,024 "Śakra" TPU chips, with a computing power scale of 400P. Over the past two years, operators have not been inactive in building intelligent computing centers, but most projects have adopted overseas GPU solutions. The policy requirement for self-reliance is one factor, but the deeper reason lies in the shift of the business model.
excerpt_i18n.es: Durante los últimos dos años, el crecimiento de los servicios de comunicación tradicionales se ha ralentizado, y los operadores han centrado su atención en la potencia de cálculo de IA. China Telecom, China Mobile y China Unicom han anunciado sucesivamente planes a gran escala para la construcción de centros de computación inteligente, y la inversión en potencia de cálculo como porcentaje del gasto de capital ha aumentado año tras año. En esta ola de transformación, la elección del chip de cálculo por parte de los operadores no solo determina la estructura de costes de su propio negocio de computación, sino que también influye en gran medida en la dirección de la industria nacional de potencia de cálculo. Actualmente, la industria nacional de potencia de cálculo de IA ya presenta un panorama de convivencia paralela de múltiples rutas tecnológicas, como TPU, GPU y ASIC. En la construcción de computación inteligente, los operadores también están pasando gradualmente de depender exclusivamente de soluciones de GPU a optar por una gama más diversificada de opciones de cálculo.
